title: Henderson's personnel and Horace Henderson's shout choruses
summary: Thomas lists the Henderson band's sections, including Russell Smith, Red Allen, Hilton Jefferson, Procope, Bailey and Hawkins. Horace wrote the out choruses, such as his hit chorus on Stealin' Apples.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Fletcher Henderson's house. (something about Russell Lewis and Joe's brother, first trumpet player with the band) So this particular day I was pretty good chops ... and that was, a lot of good guys in the band you might remember... brass section, Russell, Red and me, Russell playing first, I was playing second and Red was playing third. Hilton Jefferson playing first alto, Procope, Buster Bailey, Coleman Hawkins, Russell Toco (?) ... Walter Johnson, John Kirby and Horace Henderson.
And the trombones were who, Claude?
Claude Jones and Key Johnson. Thank you, thank you.
Horace had a way of arranging for the out chorus, what we used to shout choruses, always beautiful. Well, now it becomes (a power of a kind.) (Let me make a shout poster (?)) (The lead has changed.)
You would be playing the lead?
Yeah. But, by that time Hawkins was the one, I think he went over there to Jack Hilton Henderson, wasn't he?
That's what he meant. Power in those outposts (?). out choruses
Yeah, that explains that. I figured it was something like that Horace Hawk was horns are so funny because he wouldn't be specific but he would insist on certain things when you were recording.
Well, he was a tremendous person.
Oh, sure and you know I always naturally thought well you don't say that without a reason.
Yeah, he must have had a reason.
... Fats Waller had a tune called 'Stealin' See Them Apples.' So that my chorus, the out chorus was my chorus. It was a hit arrangement.
